17.1.intro: AI assistants (chat AI tools) work much better when they know about your business.

steps.say: Make a project in your AI assistant. Most chat AI tools have a project (or similar) space for your files. First check its data settings and turn off training on your chats if you can.
steps.check: You have an empty project for your store.
steps.lost: Look for a projects or files option in the side menu.

steps.say: Upload your brand core (Module 4), customer profiles, offers, cost drivers (Module 1), how-you-do-things notes, and past winning ads and emails.
steps.check: The project holds your business info.

steps.say: Update the files whenever something changes.
steps.check: Answers stay up to date with your business.
steps.lost: Changed a price? Update the file.

17.2.intro: A few jobs save the most time with AI. Always read and fix what AI writes before you use it.

steps.say: Use AI for ads: hooks, scripts, briefs, ad text versions, picture layouts, resizing, and finding which parts of your ads win.
steps.check: Your next batch of ads is drafted faster.

steps.say: Use AI for email: campaign drafts, subject lines and flow emails.
steps.check: Email drafts take minutes, not hours.

steps.say: Use AI for the website: section text, FAQs, landing page drafts, page checks, and digging into exported data when sales drop.
steps.check: Site words and checks are quicker.

steps.say: Use AI for admin: ad account naming, search term reviews, support replies, invoice entry and stock reports.
steps.lost: Ask AI to draft one support reply.

steps.say: Set up an AI support helper for "where is my order?" and common questions. It must hand anything sensitive to a person.
steps.lost: Start with "where is my order?" only.

17.3.intro: Connectors let AI read your data. Agents can take steps for you. Anything that changes something must be approved by a person.

steps.say: Connect AI only through official integrations that follow platform rules.
steps.check: AI can read your data without risking a policy flag.
steps.careful: Unofficial automation tools on ad accounts can trigger policy flags or bans.

steps.say: Set every write action (anything that changes something) to need your approval.
steps.check: Nothing changes in your accounts without your click.

17.4.intro: AI is powerful, but it makes mistakes. These rules keep you safe.

steps.say: Never paste passwords or access tokens into an AI chat.
Check every claim AI writes, especially health and before-and-after claims.
steps.check: Nothing false goes out under your name.
steps.lost: Read it. Is every claim true?

steps.say: Label AI-made people and voices where rules need it. Report fakes of your content or face to the platform, with proof.
steps.check: You follow the rules and protect your brand.

17.5.intro: Helix follows the same rules. Maths uses fixed rules, AI only writes short text, and nothing changes without your OK.

steps.say: Helix uses fixed rules for all maths (profit, MER, break-even). So the numbers are always exact.
steps.check: You can trust every number on the Dashboard.
steps.lost: Helix maths is fixed rules, not guesses.

steps.say: Helix only uses AI to write short text when you press the button: a store check summary, ad copy drafts and "I'm lost" answers. Each plan has a monthly allowance. It runs on Gemini 2.5 Flash-Lite with prompt training turned off, so your data does not train AI models.
steps.check: You know Helix's numbers and plan come from plain rules. AI text is a draft you read first.
steps.lost: AI in Helix only writes drafts. The maths is fixed rules.

steps.say: Approve or reject each action in **Waiting for your OK**. New campaigns are made as paused drafts that you switch on.
steps.check: Every change in your accounts has your OK.
